subject: Hosted API latency: measurement windowing and aggregation clarification for Clearwater
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@clearwater.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>; Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clearwater.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify p50/p95 measurement for Hosted API in draft SLO addendum

Hi Vivek / Monica,

Thanks for the draft SLO addendum you shared last week. Our engineering and procurement teams reviewed it and had a couple of follow-ups specifically around how p50 and p95 are measured and how short-lived bursts are handled. Two things jumped out: 

- The draft ties p95 to a 15-minute sliding window, reported every 5 minutes. Given our traffic pattern (short, frequent bursts for batch imports), our ops team is worried that a few 15-minute windows in a month could push us over the threshold and trigger credits.

- We need clarity on whether regional routing/fallbacks (e.g., to a cheaper model variant) count as a failure for latency SLO purposes. On our side we want predictable billing and to avoid disputes where transient routing decisions are treated as SLO violations.

Specific asks: 
1) Can Redwood provide an example of how a burst affecting three 15-minute windows would be aggregated and whether there are transient carveouts?
2) Can you confirm whether cross-region fallback counts towards p95 violations or whether it is excluded under the planned graceful-degradation carveouts?

We'd like to get this resolved before legal signs the contract next week. Attached is a spreadsheet with our monthly 95th percentile examples for a sample month — hope that helps.

Thanks,
Sanjay Mehta
Head of Platform Engineering
Clearwater Systems

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 12:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 measurement for Hosted API in draft SLO addendum

Sanjay — thanks for the clear notes and the example sheet. Quick answers up front, then a proposal: 

1) Aggregation model: we calculate p50/p95 over a rolling 15-minute window (standard), but SLO enforcement is based on the monthly aggregation across windows. We do not treat every single 15-minute violation as an immediate credit — credits are applied when the monthly rolling aggregate crosses the committed threshold. In practice that means short burst-driven blips rarely result in credits unless they meaningfully move the monthly distribution.

2) Cross-region fallback: we treat routing decisions as part of normal operation. However, for customers with dedicated capacity we can carve out forced cross-region fallbacks that are explicitly triggered by capacity constraints. For hosted customers, normal automatic fallback is considered operational and counts toward latency unless the fallback was customer-requested or explicitly documented as an incident (e.g., a region-level outage).

Proposal we can put into an addendum: 
- Measurement windows: p50/p95 computed per 15-minute sliding windows, sampled every 5 minutes.
- Monthly enforcement: we compute the monthly distribution from those windows; credits trigger only when the monthly p95/p50 exceeds the commitment for more than one billing cycle's worth of impact (we can define this as crossing the threshold for >=0.5% of total 15-minute windows in the month).
- Transient carveout: automatic routing changes due to transient backend congestion (lasting < 30s) will be excluded from monthly enforcement; longer fallbacks count unless labeled as part of a Redwood incident.

I'm looping in Karthik and Marissa to validate from product and legal. If that sounds reasonable to you, we'll draft the specific language for the addendum and attach examples showing how a three-burst month would (and would not) move the monthly p95.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: SLO-addendum-draft.docx (word doc, 95KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 measurement for Hosted API in draft SLO addendum

Hey all — quick product note to make sure examples match runtime behavior. Two operational clarifications: 

- The 30s transient carveout Vivek mentioned should be implemented as a client-observable prefix cache/grace period. For streaming requests we maintain continuity and do not split windows mid-stream.

- For the monthly threshold example: we should use absolute window counts in the addendum language rather than percentages to keep calculations transparent. I suggest: credits apply if monthly windows over threshold >= 50 windows (i.e., ~25 hours of impacted 15-minute windows) unless the windows are attributable to a documented Redwood incident. This avoids tiny percentages that are hard to audit.

I've attached a small spreadsheet with three hypothetical months showing: (A) short burst pattern that does not trigger credits, (B) repeated sustained degradation that does, (C) a region outage that we classify as a Redwood incident and exclude. Sanjay — can you confirm your team is OK with a 50-window threshold approach?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product, Hosted Inference
Redwood Inference

Vivek / Karthik — thanks, this is helpful. Procurement is comfortable proceeding if the addendum includes: 

- The 15-minute window sampling and monthly aggregation language you proposed.
- The 50-window absolute threshold for triggering credits (please include a short worked example in the addendum).
- The transient carveout described (routing changes <30s excluded) and a clear definition of what counts as a Redwood incident.

Marissa — can you draft redline language we can share with our legal team? Monica — can you confirm the billing team will accept the 50-window rule? If yes, we'll finalize and sign.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sanjay
Head of Platform Engineering
Clearwater Systems
